neighbours.label: a pronoun or relative word ('that', 'they', 'it', 'which') that opens a clause modifying the noun just before it
fire: I look forward to the swallows every spring for the news they bring.
We finally bridged the distance that had kept our families apart.
Imagine swinging a heavy hammer like a golf club that weighs forty pounds.
In an earlier project, a smart lamp that we built with students, we used sensors.
She kept the letters he wrote during the war in a tin box.
The village has a well which has never run dry.
He returned the book it took him three years to finish.
They fixed the bridge that the flood had damaged.
quiet: I look forward to the swallows every spring because they are lovely.
We finally bridged the distance between our two families.
Imagine swinging a heavy hammer like a golf club on a sunny day.
In an earlier project with students, we used sensors in a smart lamp.
She kept the old wartime letters in a tin box.
The village has an old well in the main square.
He returned the long book to the library on Friday.
They fixed the old bridge after the flood.

notes: card flags broad (1.5% >0.1 max); ' that', ' this', ' they', ' it', ' which' after a noun phrase
